documents.title: Academic Honesty Guide: Honesty in Academic Work
documents.summary: The college-wide honesty policy treats AI as an outside source that must be cited and acknowledged. Uncited LLM text is a violation, instructors may set stricter assignment rules, and the document also lays out the review, outcome and appeal process.
documents.stance_why: The policy never bans AI; it names uncited use of an LLM as a violation ("Quoting or paraphrasing language from a Large Language Model (LLM) or other AI service without citing") and requires acknowledging "assistance received from ... a Large Language Model or AI service". AI is therefore allowed when acknowledged, with instructors setting extra rules, so permit.

units.why: The sentence names the core wrong as misrepresenting another's effort, "whether derived from a machine-generated source or a person", as your own, so it is the definition of the misconduct AI use can fall under. P36 (AI misrepresentation handled as academic dishonesty) fits better than P61, which would need a definition of AI or of the policy's scope.

units.frag_start: Fundamentally, violation of these principles misrepresents
units.policy: Violating academic honesty principles means misrepresenting another's intellectual effort, whether derived from a machine-generated source or a person, as your own.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: student/general/informs/P36. Coder B: all/general/informs/P61. The passage defines the honesty violation and only mentions machine-generated sources in passing; it does not define AI or the policy scope, so P61 does not fit. The text addresses students ("as your own"), so actor is student.

units.why: The list of violations includes "Quoting or paraphrasing language from a Large Language Model (LLM) or other AI service without citing", making uncited AI text an academic honesty violation. P36 fits (classified as misconduct); P24 is about the duty to disclose, whereas this sentence classifies the failure as a violation.

notes: The CS department's own academic integrity policy (referenced by course handouts as https://www.cs.grinnell.edu/academic-integrity) returns 404, also in Wayback, so computing is marked inaccessible; recheck for a moved URL. CSC 151 syllabi from the known list are deferred. The guide overview page (node/49236) added no policy text. Art History has a departmental AI policy but is not computing. Coder B: uncovered units are the rule barring instructors from discussing suspected violations with students (two docs), the evidence standard, and the non-contract clause. Reconciler: no new types proposed. Dropped B-only units: fabricated-citation line (no AI mention), closed-book and independent-work defaults (no AI mention), non-contract clause (boilerplate).
